findings.text: follow-on: the new reportless branch reads the row only when the exception carries no rollback report, but every staging refusal in _commit_landing_writes raises through _landing_refusal (promotion_scope.py:2215), which always sets LANDING_ROLLBACK_ATTRIBUTE; the recorded incident's own landing record docs-state/reckon/runs/r-20261019T080250830060.landing.json shows the refusal carried a report whose ledger entry read true (reverted), which the base code maps to the re-promote wording, so the branch this change adds may not be the branch the recorded incident exercised.

follow-on: the first case reaches the reportless branch by monkeypatching _landing_refusal to drop the rollback report, a state production cannot produce from a staging refusal and cannot produce with an absent row from a post-commit failure, so the guard reddens on the mutation but exercises a synthetic state rather than the incident's code path.
